# Cairn System Notes

## Basic Pulse Mechanism
A pulse adds marks to a cairn based on two components: a fixed stride value, plus bonus marks equal to how many complete strides fit into the current height. The taller the cairn already is, the more a pulse adds to it. This creates accelerating growth.

## Multiple Pulses
When applying multiple pulses sequentially, each pulse is calculated based on the new height from the previous pulse. The cairn grows progressively larger with each cycle, and the amount added per pulse increases as the height increases.

## Drains and Leaks
After a pulse, a cairn can lose marks through a leak or drain. A leak removes a fixed number of marks. When cycles repeat (pulse followed by leak), the net effect depends on whether the pulse growth exceeds the leak loss. Eventually, if the leak is large enough relative to the pulse growth, the cairn will reach zero or go negative.

## Reverse Engineering Starting Heights
Given a final height after multiple pulses, you can work backwards by testing candidate starting heights and applying pulses forward until you match the final height.

## Merging Cairns
Two cairns can be combined using weighted shares (expressed as fractions or tenths). Each cairn contributes its height multiplied by its share percentage. A tether value (which can be positive or negative) is added or subtracted from the final merged result. The tether can reduce or increase the final merged height.
